text:
alex: Hey team — getting multiple reports from a customer that their p95/p99 for our /v1/chat.function_call endpoint spiked ~3x after yesterday's deploy. They say normal traffic is fine but any request that triggers tool routing + structured-output validation jumps to 800–1200ms at p95. Can someone triage?

marina: looping in eng-runtime + SRE. Do we have any perf dashboards for tool-router paths?

chris: saw the alert in the latency dashboard at ~2024-11-12T22:15Z. Topline: p50 ~80ms unchanged, p95 jumped from ~220ms -> ~760ms, p99 to ~1.2s. This matches the customer's window.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-4289 latency spike on tool-router validation. Pager schedule: oncall=sre-weekend.

alex: customer provided a sample request and said the slowdown only happens when we return structured JSON in our tool call output and we run schema validation before routing. Repro curl in thread below.

alex: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat.function_call 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4r","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"call_tool get_order --order_id 1234"}],"functions":[{"name":"get_order","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"}},"required":["order_id"]}}],"return_tool_output":true}'
| jq '.meta.latency'
```

alex: customer ran load test (50 rps sustained for 5m) and saw consistent p95 regressions only for tool calls that hit our schema validation path.

marina: we shipped a change in https://github.com/redwood-inc/runtime/commit/8d9f3a that added synchronous JSON schema validation inside the request thread to avoid delayed failures. The intent was to fail fast, but it sounds like CPU/serialization is adding latency.

chris: code excerpt from the deploy: ```python
# blocking validation inserted inline
validated = jsonschema.validate(parsed_output, schema)
# then route to tool router
route = router.pick(validated)
```

chris: note: validation uses jsonschema (Python) which is not JIT-optimized. Under moderate concurrency it spawns CPU pressure on the worker threads and blocks the event loop.

eva: confirmed via flame graphs: the validation step accounts for ~45% of p95 cost during the spike window. We see increased sys CPU on model-serving nodes, esp at tail. Link: https://perf.redwood/internal/flame/INC-4289 (internal).

marina: immediate mitigation options?

chris: short-term: rollback the inline validation change (revert commit 8d9f3a) to restore previous behavior where validation was handled asynchronously by a background verifier. That will remove blocking CPU from request path.

alex: customer asked for a hotfix rather than full rollback — they want validation but not at tail cost. Any cheaper options?

eva: we could sample validation for the heavy flows: validate 1% of responses and otherwise accept output as-is. Not ideal but buys time.

marina: other option: move validation to a shared worker pool (separate process) and do async validation with streaming responses: return tool call response immediately, mark response as "pending validation", and if validation fails post a follow-up callback or warning. That requires client support for async callbacks.

chris: long-term: replace jsonschema with a compiled C library (like ajv for Node or faster C-based validator) or pre-compile validators per-schema to speed checks. Also memoize schema->validator for repeated calls.

alex: customer is sensitive because they rely on immediate validated tool outputs to avoid downstream errors. Need a plan that both reduces tail and preserves guarantees.

marina: proposed immediate plan: 1) revert inline blocking change on runtime (hotfix) 2) re-deploy with async validation worker pool + optimistic return on tool router for critical customers (feature flag) 3) accelerate replacing validator implementation and add per-schema compiled validators + caching.

chris: agreed. I can open the revert PR now, run canary for 30m, and monitor p95. If green we push to prod.

deploy-bot: Release 2024.11.12-hotfix-1 deployed to canary (sha: a7c9e2) by chris.

sre-bot: Canary monitoring: p95 tool-router latency dropped from 760ms -> 210ms within 10 minutes of canary. No error rate increase.

alex: customer confirmed latency improved on their end after canary reached them. Thanks. They still want validation but ask we not impact tail.

marina: follow-ups created: TICKET-5934 (async validator worker pool design), TICKET-5935 (benchmark compiled validator libs), TICKET-5936 (client async callback API for pending validation). Assigning to chris/eva/infra.

eva: small perf notes for the tickets: - measure median validation time per schema size; - add histogram for schema-validation CPU; - add metric "validation.sync_latency" to trace path.

chris: repro steps in case someone needs to retest locally: 1) start runtime locally with DEBUG_VALIDATION_SYNC=1 2) run the curl from above with a heavy schema (schema with many nested properties and enums) 3) run `htop` to watch CPU on the worker thread and `strace -c` if needed 4) compare timings with DEBUG_VALIDATION_SYNC=0.

alex: customer-facing message drafted: "We identified a regression introduced during a safety-related change that made JSON schema validation synchronous in the request path. We’ve rolled back the change and are working on a shorter-term async validator and longer-term performance fixes. We'll follow up with timelines." Sent to customer.

marina: good. Any objections to making the sync validation a gated feature flag so we can enable it for low-traffic enterprise accounts where correctness matters more than latency?

eva: sounds reasonable. Feature flag + quotas so validation compute doesn't create noisy neighbor issues. Also add an adaptive sampling rate that ramps validation on/off based on current latency budget.

chris: i'll keep monitoring the dashboard. Will update tickets with benchmarks and estimated ETA for compiled validator (2 weeks dev + 1 week testing).

alex: thanks everyone. Closing loop with the customer and marking INC-4289 resolved for now.

marina: noting lessons: avoid heavy CPU ops inline on hot request paths; prefer async or compiled validators; add p95/p99 tests for structured-output flows in our canary suite.

alex: +1 on adding structured-output scenarios to canary. Also adding a regression alert specifically for tool-router tail latency.

chris: added alert: "tool-router.validation.p99 > 900ms for 5m" -> P2.

sre-bot: Incident INC-4289 status: Resolved.

alex: thanks all :thumbsup:
